answer.rationale: With only 14 days before contract expiry and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching primary vendors now carries unacceptable delivery risk—memory_c2 explicitly warns the low-cost vendor missed SLA in 3 of 4 quarters and should not be sole-sourced for a critical line. Adding a second source is valuable (memory_c3) but requires qualification time we don't have this cycle. Deferring is unavailable since this is a critical, expiring contract, not the non-critical case in memory_c5. Renegotiating with the incumbent (memory_c4, memory_c6) has a track record of recovering real margin and even unlocking volume discounts without narrowing service scope, directly addressing the 18% cost mandate while preserving the stable integration and delivery continuity seen in memory_c1. I verified c4 and c2 because they most directly bear on whether negotiation can meet the cost target and why switching is currently too risky. This is a single-cycle stopgap: full resolution of cost-vs-risk tradeoffs (e.g., building a qualified second source) should be revisited next review.
